'''Barbara Anne Croy''' {{post-nominal|FCAHS|FRSC}} (née '''McLeish''') is a Canadian reproductive immunologist and [[professor emerita]] in Biomedical and Molecular Sciences at [[Queen's University at Kingston|Queen's University]]. From 2004 until 2016, Croy was a [[Canada Research Chair]] in Reproduction, Development and Sexual Function. In 2017, she was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Canada]]. Her research focus is on mice pregnancy and [[natural killer cells]].

==Early life and career==
Croy was born to parents Laura Agnes and Ed McLeish as Barbara Anne McLeish.{{failed verification|date=June 2019}}<ref>{{cite web |title=Laura Agnes (née Richardson) McLeish |url=http://www.yourlifemoments.ca/sitepages/Obituary.asp?oId=369990 |website=yourlifemoments.ca |date=February 27, 2010}}</ref> Barbara Anne McLeish was born in 1946 in [[London, Ontario]].<ref name="thesis-croy-1974" />

After finding success in science during high school, Croy decided to pursue a career as a veterinarian. She attended the [[University of Guelph]] to partake in their veterinary courses.<ref name = ":1">{{cite web |last1=Lefebvre |first1=Samantha |title=Interview With a Reproductive Biologist: A Closer Look at the Life and Work of Dr. Anne Croy |url=https://www.jyi.org/2017-february/interview-with-a-reproductive-biologist-a-closer-look-at-the-life-and-work-of-dr-anne-croy |website=Journal of Young Investigators |accessdate=April 21, 2019 |date=February 1, 2017}}</ref> Croy was one of three women in her graduating class.<ref name = "chrcrm">{{cite web |title=Tales from the Mouse Lady |url=https://chrcrm.org/en/rotm/dr-anne-croy |website=chrcrm.org |accessdate=May 16, 2019 |date=August 2013}}</ref>

After receiving her DVM from the University of Guelph in 1969, Croy went immediately to work under the directions of [[Ernest McCulloch]] and David Osoba at the [[University of Toronto]] where she was awarded a PhD in 1974.<ref name="thesis-croy-1974">{{cite thesis |url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/302758224/ |title=Studies on The Immune Responses Of Athymic Mice. |date=1974 |publisher=[[University of Toronto]] |degree=Ph.D. |last=Croy |first=Barbara Anne |id={{ProQuest|302758224}} |url-access=subscription}}</ref> She went on to become the first nonmedical doctor to earn her PhD at the [[University of Toronto]]'s  Institute of Medical Sciences. After graduating with her PhD, Croy and her husband operated their own veterinary practice in [[St. Catharines]], [[Ontario]] from 1975 to 1997.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |date=August 25, 2006 |title=Biographies for Recipients of the 2006 ASRI Awards |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1600-0897.2006.00427.x |journal=American Journal of Reproductive Immunology |language=en |volume=56 |issue=4 |pages=215–217 |doi=10.1111/j.1600-0897.2006.00427.x |pmid=16938109 |issn=1046-7408 |via=Wiley Online Library|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name = ":2">{{cite web |last1=Anderson |first1=Gayle |title=A Passion for Research |url=https://atrium.lib.uoguelph.ca/xmlui/bitstream/handle/10214/11700/ug_atguelphvol44_issue5_2000.pdf?sequence=1 |website=atrium.lib.uoguelph.ca |accessdate=May 16, 2019 |date=March 15, 2000}}</ref>

From 1985 to 2004, Croy worked in Guelph's [[Ontario Veterinary College]] (OVC).<ref name = ":2"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Ontario Veterinary College Alumni Association Annual Report |url=http://ovc.uoguelph.ca/alumni/documents/OVCAA_2018AnnualReport.pdf |website=ovc.uoguelph.ca |accessdate=April 21, 2019 |page=12}}</ref> She worked as an associate professor in Biomedical Sciences<ref name = "RSC bio">{{cite web |title=Royal Society of Canada Eastern Ontario Regional Seminar |url=http://www.cimvhr.ca/documents/RSC%202018%20Seminar%20Bios.pdf |website=cimvhr.ca |accessdate=May 16, 2019}}</ref> and was granted tenure by the university in 1988.<ref>{{cite news|title=Promotion and Tenure|newspaper=At Guelph| volume= 32|date= June 1, 1988 |pages=1–2|url=https://archive.org/details/p2atguelphvol32uofg/page/n97}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Macdonald |first1=Kerri |title=The best laid plans of mice & men |url=https://www.queensjournal.ca/story/2009-01-29/features/best-laid-plans-mice-and-men/ |accessdate=May 16, 2019 |publisher=Queen's Journal |date=January 29, 2009}}</ref> While at Guelph, she mentored 35 students working on research projects in the Biomedical Sciences to achieve their undergraduate honors degree.<ref name=":0" /> After earning a placement at [[Princess Margaret Cancer Centre|Princess Margaret Hospital]], Croy became the first woman in their department of biomedical sciences to earn a PhD.<ref name = ":1"/> Her work at the hospital focused on the immune system of mice.<ref name = "chrcrm"/> Due to her research in biomedical reproduction, Croy became a  permanent study section member of the [[National Institutes of Health]].<ref name = ":2"/>

In 1993, she was awarded the Smith Kline Beecham Annual Health Trust Award for Research Excellence.<ref>{{cite news|title=Awards|newspaper=At Guelph| volume= 37|date= March 31, 1993|page=2|url=https://archive.org/details/p2atguelphvol37uofg/page/n13 }}</ref> The following year, she began teaching a graduate course on fetal health at OVC.<ref name = ":2"/> In 1995, Croy accepted a research lab position at [[Brock University]] studying functional immune cells in mouse uterus while continuing her graduate studies at the university. She later accepted a position at the University of Guelph teaching the anatomy of cows and horses.<ref name = "chrcrm"/> She collaborated with Betty-Anne McBey to examine the purpose of [[natural killer cells]] in the uterus of pregnant women through mice experiments.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Anne LeBold |author2=Jeff Stuart |title=Cell sorter enhances research in plant, animal biotechnology |url=https://atrium.lib.uoguelph.ca/xmlui/bitstream/handle/10214/11019/ug_atguelphvol39_issue26_1995.pdf?sequence=1&isAllowed=y |accessdate=May 20, 2019 |page=5 |date=July 12, 1995}}</ref> In 1999, while working at the university, Croy was awarded the J.C.B. Grant Senior Scientist Award from the Canadian Association for Anatomy, Neurobiology and Cell Biology.<ref>{{cite web |title=Alumni Take Centre Stage |url=https://atrium.lib.uoguelph.ca/xmlui/bitstream/handle/10214/11683/ug_atguelphvol43_issues11to21_1999.txt?sequence=2&isAllowed=y |website=atrium.lib.uoguelph.ca |accessdate=May 19, 2019 |date=1999}}</ref>

In the early 2000s, Croy began working as an [[adjunct professor]] at [[Roswell Park Comprehensive Cancer Center]] in [[Buffalo, New York]] after receiving funding for her research with natural killer cells.<ref>{{cite web |title=OVMA Honours Service to Veterinary Medicine |url=https://atrium.lib.uoguelph.ca/xmlui/bitstream/handle/10214/11740/ug_atguelphvol46_issues1to10_2002.txt?sequence=2&isAllowed=y |website=atrium.lib.uoguelph.ca |accessdate=May 20, 2019 |date=2002}}</ref> On January 24, 2002, Croy was awarded the Award of Merit from the [[Ontario Veterinary Medical Association]].<ref>{{cite journal |date=2002|pmc=339265 |title=People in the News · des Gens, des Nouvelles|journal=The Canadian Veterinary Journal|volume=43|issue=5|pages=345–346}}</ref>

Croy left the University of Guelph in 2004 after being named a [[Canada Research Chair]] in Reproduction, Development and Sexual Function at [[Queen's University at Kingston|Queen's University]].<ref>{{cite web |title=2016 Workshop Faculty |url=http://www.queensu.ca/workshops/placenta/?q=node/3 |website=queensu.ca |accessdate=May 16, 2019}}</ref>

==Later career==
In 2005, Croy published "''A Review of Trafficking and Activation of Uterine Natural Killer Cells.''"<ref>{{cite journal |title=A Review of Trafficking and Activation of Uterine Natural Killer Cells |journal=American Journal of Reproductive Immunology |volume=54 |issue=6 |pages=322–331 |pmc=2967519 |year=2005 |last1=Van Den Heuvel |first1=M. J. |last2=Xie |first2=X. |last3=Tayade |first3=C. |last4=Peralta |first4=C. |last5=Fang |first5=Y. |last6=Leonard |first6=S. |last7=Paffaro Jr |first7=V. A. |last8=Sheikhi |first8=A.K. |last9=Murrant |first9=C. |last10=Croy |first10=B. A. |pmid=16305657 |doi=10.1111/j.1600-0897.2005.00336.x }}</ref> The following year, she was awarded the [[American Journal of Reproductive Immunology]] award by the [[American Society for Reproductive Immunology]].<ref>{{cite web |title=American Journal of Reproductive Immunology Award |url=https://theasri.org/page-1075405 |website=theasri.org |accessdate=May 17, 2019}}</ref> She was also the 2007 recipient of the Munsgaard
Blackwell award for outstanding publication in the field of reproduction immunology from the American Society for Reproductive Immunology.<ref>{{cite web |title=Queen's University Annual Report 2007 |url=https://www.queensu.ca/financialservices/sites/webpublish.queensu.ca.finwww/files/files/reports/annualreport/AnnualReport2007.pdf |website=queensu.ca |accessdate=May 17, 2019 |page=25}}</ref>

In 2010, Croy renewed her position as Canada Research Chair and received $1.4 million over seven years to fund her study on early pregnancy, the regulation of gestational blood pressure, and post-partum immune memory effects.<ref>{{cite news |last1=John |first1=Robert |title=Queen's Receives $9.1 Million in Canada Research Chairs Funding |url=http://kingstonherald.com/release/queens-receives-canada-research-chairs-funding-201032892 |accessdate=May 17, 2019 |publisher=Kingston Herald |date=November 25, 2010}}</ref> The following year, she collaborated with [[Aureo Yamada]] and International Trade Canada to create a federally-funded student exchange program centered around maternal health knowledge.<ref>{{cite news |author1=Meaghan Wray |title=New student exchange |url=https://www.queensjournal.ca/story/2011-10-28/news/new-student-exchange/ |accessdate=May 20, 2019 |publisher=The Queen's Journal |date=October 28, 2011}}</ref> In 2012, she was named a Fellow of the [[Canadian Academy of Health Sciences]] due to her research on maternal and infant health during pregnancy.<ref>{{cite web |title=Senate Research Report |url=https://www.queensu.ca/secretariat/sites/webpublish.queensu.ca.uslcwww/files/files/senate/agendasminutes/103012/Oct30_12AppM.pdf |website=queensu.ca |accessdate=April 21, 2019 |date=October 30, 2012}}</ref> She subsequently published "''The Guide to Investigation of Mouse Pregnancy''" in 2014<ref>{{cite book |title=The Guide to Investigation of Mouse Pregnancy |url=https://www.elsevier.com/books/the-guide-to-investigation-of-mouse-pregnancy/croy/978-0-12-394445-0 |website=elsevier.com |year= 2013 |isbn=978-0-12-394445-0 |accessdate=May 20, 2019 |last1=Anne Croy |first1=B. |last2=Yamada |first2=Aureo T. |last3=Demayo |first3=Francesco J. |last4=Lee Adamson |first4=S. |publisher=Elsevier Science }}</ref> and received funding to research reproductive health and apply policy suggestions.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Craig |first1=Anne |title=Funding strengthens leading-edge research |url=https://www.queensu.ca/news/articles/funding-strengthens-leading-edge-research |website=queensu.ca |accessdate=May 20, 2019 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140424121809/https://www.queensu.ca/news/articles/funding-strengthens-leading-edge-research |archivedate=April 24, 2014 |date=April 14, 2014}}</ref>

In 2015, she earned Queen University's Prizes for Excellence in Research<ref>{{cite web |title=Dr. Anne Croy |url=https://www.queensu.ca/vpr/eaffect/spring-summer-2016/anne-croy |website=queensu.ca |accessdate=April 21, 2019 |date=2016}}</ref> but rescinded her position as Canada Research Chair in 2016.<ref name = "RSC bio"/> The next year, Croy was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Canada]] for her work with [[Natural killer cell#NK cell function in pregnancy|uterine NK cells during pregnancy]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Dr. Anne Croy elected to the Royal Society of Canada |url=https://healthsci.queensu.ca/node/714 |website=healthsci.queensu.ca |accessdate=April 21, 2019 |date=September 7, 2017}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Croy met her husband Carl Croy while studying veterinary medicine at the University of Guelph. Before his death in 2017, they had two children together.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dr. Carl Croy |url=https://jamesreidfuneralhome.com/tribute/details/421/Dr-Carl-Croy/obituary.html |website=jamesreidfuneralhome.com |accessdate=May 16, 2019}}</ref>
